traverse: Traverse the module graph rooted at `entry`, which must be a WHATWG `URL` instance. `readModule` is called with a `URL` instance for every module to be read and must either return the module source, if it exists, or `null`. `listPrefix` is called with a `URL` instance of every prefix to be listed and must yield `URL` instances that have the specified `URL` as a prefix. If not provided, prefixes won't be traversed. If `readModule` returns a promise or `listPrefix` returns a promise generator, synchronous iteration is not supported.
default: The default resolver, which simply forwards to <https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-module-resolve> and <https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-addon-resolve> with the literal options passed by the caller.
bare: The Bare resolver, which matches the options used by the Bare module system.
node: The Node.js resolver, which matches the options used by the Node.js module system.
traverse.link: Resolve one import and record the result in `imports`. Before that, it resolves the specifier of each of the `imports` and `wasi` attributes of `entry` as a module and records it in `imports` too. The `wasi` attribute is new in v2.6.0. See [The `host` and `wasi` import attributes](#the-host-and-wasi-import-attributes).
TraverseOptions:
`mount` is the URL that the entry is mounted at when it is a bundle, for a consumer that loads the bundle with an explicit mount. The addons and assets that the bundle declares resolve relative to it. It defaults to the URL of the entry itself, and it applies only to the entry, not to bundles that the entry imports. Added in v2.7.1. See [Bundled addons and assets](#bundled-addons-and-assets).

`conditions` is passed to the resolver. As of v2.7.0, the traversal first adds the conditions of the host under a `host` attribute; see [Conditions under a `host` attribute](#conditions-under-a-host-attribute). The default resolver forwards `conditions` to `bare-module-resolve` and `bare-addon-resolve` unchanged. As of v2.7.0, [`resolve.bare`](#bare-module-traverseresolvebare) and [`resolve.node`](#bare-module-traverseresolvenode) add it to the conditions of each host, where before they ignored it.

As of v2.7.0, `TraverseOptions` extends [`ResolveOptions`](#resolveoptions), so it also lists the options of `bare-module-resolve`, such as `defer` and `imports`. Before, it listed only the options of `bare-addon-resolve`, although the traversal already passed options such as `defer` and `imports` on to the resolver.
Dependency: `wasi` is the URL of the WASI provider of a WebAssembly addon, when its importer named one with the `wasi` import attribute. The traversal has set it since v2.6.0, and the type declares it as of v2.7.2. A module imported under several `host` or `wasi` attributes is walked once for each, so the same `url` can be yielded in more than one `Dependency`. See [WebAssembly addons](#webassembly-addons).
